# Baruch Chapter 6 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
## [The Letter of Jeremiah]

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Baruch 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/BAR_006_page_001.jpg

---

**1** A copy of the letter that Jeremiah sent to those who were to be led captive to Babylon by the king of the Babylonians, to give them the message that God commanded him.

**2** Because of the sins that you have committed before God, you will be led away captive to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar, king of the Babylonians.

**3** When you come to Babylon you will remain there for many years, for a long time, up to seven generations; after that I will bring you back from there in peace.

**4** And now in Babylon you will see gods made of silver and gold and wood, carried on shoulders, inspiring awe among the nations.

**5** Beware, therefore, of becoming like the foreigners; do not let fear of them take hold of you

**6** when you see the crowd before and behind them worshipping them. But say in your heart: You are the one who should be worshipped, O Lord.

**7** For my angel is with you, and he himself is watching over your lives.

**8** For their tongues have been polished by a craftsman, and they themselves are gilded and silvered; but they are false and cannot speak.

**9** And as for an offering to them of gold as if for a girl who loves ornaments —

**10** the priests take away from their gods gold and silver and use it for themselves.

**11** They even give from it to prostitutes on the roof of the temple, and they deck out these gods, these wooden, silvered, and gilded ones, with garments like human beings.

**12** Yet these gods cannot save themselves from rust and moth, though they are wrapped in purple robes.

**13** They wipe their faces on account of the dust of the temple, which is thick upon them.

**14** He who cannot put to death anyone who sins against him wields a scepter like a judge of a land;

**15** he has a dagger in his right hand and an axe; but he cannot deliver himself from war and robbers.

**16** From this it is evident that they are not gods; so do not fear them.

**17** For just as a vessel that a man uses is of no use when it is broken, so are their gods: when they have been set up in their temples, their eyes are full of dust stirred up by the feet of those who come in.

**18** And just as the gates are shut on every side against anyone who has offended a king, as being under sentence of death, so the priests secure the temples with doors and locks and bolts, in case they are plundered by robbers.

**19** They light lamps for them — more than they light for themselves — though they cannot see a single one.

**20** They are just like a beam of the house; men say their hearts are eaten away; when the creeping things from the earth devour them and their garments, they do not feel it.

**21** Their faces are blackened by the smoke that comes from the temple.

**22** Bats and swallows and the birds alight on their bodies and heads; and cats do likewise.

**23** From this you will know that they are not gods; so do not fear them.

**24** The gold with which they are adorned for beauty — unless someone wipes off the tarnish, they will not shine; for even when they were being cast, they had no feeling.

**25** They are bought without regard to price; and there is no breath in them.

**26** Having no feet, they are carried on shoulders and display their own shame to mankind; and those who serve them are put to shame as well.

**27** If they are set on the ground, they cannot rise up; and if one tips them over, they cannot straighten themselves; offerings placed before them are like offerings placed before the dead.

**28** What is sacrificed to them their priests sell and misuse; likewise their wives salt some of it, but they give none of it to the poor or helpless.

**29** Women with their monthly flow and women giving birth touch their sacrifices; from this, knowing that they are not gods, do not fear them.

**30** For how can they be called gods? Because women serve as officiants at the shrines of the wooden, silvered, and golden gods.

**31** And in their temples the priests sit with torn tunics, with their heads and beards shaved, with their heads uncovered.

**32** They howl and shout before their gods as some do at a funeral feast.

**33** The priests take some of their garments and put them on their wives and children.

**34** Whether one does good to them or evil, they will not be able to repay it; they can neither set up a king nor remove one.

**35** Likewise they can neither give wealth nor provide money; if one makes a vow to them and does not keep it, they will not require it.

**36** They can neither save a man from death nor rescue the weak from the mighty.

**37** They cannot restore sight to a blind man; they cannot deliver a man who is in distress.

**38** They cannot show compassion to a widow or do good to an orphan.

**39** Their wooden, gilded, and silvered gods are like the stones of the mountain; those who serve them will be put to shame.

**40** How then can it be supposed or said that they are gods?

**41** Even the Chaldeans themselves dishonor them; for when they see a mute person unable to speak, they bring him before Bel and ask Bel to make him speak, as if Bel were able to understand.

**42** Yet they cannot apprehend this themselves and abandon them; for they have no sense.

**43** Women with cords around them sit along the roads, burning bran for incense; and when one of them is drawn aside by some passerby who lies with her, she ridicules her neighbor who has not been honored as she has, and has not had her cord broken.

**44** Everything to do with their gods is false; how then can it be supposed or said that they are gods?

**45** They were made by craftsmen and goldsmiths; they can be nothing other than what the craftsmen wish them to be.

**46** Those who make them can hardly live long; how then can the things they make be gods?

**47** For they have left only lies and disgrace to those who come after.

**48** For when war and calamity come upon them, the priests consult among themselves where they can hide with them.

**49** How then can one fail to understand that they are not gods, they who cannot save themselves from war and calamity?

**50** Since they are of wood, gilded and silvered, it will afterward be known that they are false; it will be manifest to all the nations and kings that they are not gods but the work of human hands, and that there is no work of God in them.

**51** Who then can fail to know that they are not gods?

**52** For they cannot set up a king over a land or give rain to people.

**53** They cannot judge their own cause or deliver one who is wronged, for they have no power; they are like crows between heaven and earth.

**54** When fire falls on the house of a wooden god with silvered and gilded ones, their priests will flee and escape, but they themselves will be burned in the midst like beams.

**55** Moreover they can withstand neither king nor enemies; how then can one accept or think that they are gods?

**56** Gods made of wood, silvered and gilded, are not able to save themselves from thieves and robbers.

**57** Anyone stronger than they will strip them of their gold and silver and of the garments they wear, and go off with it; they will not be able to help themselves.

**58** So it is better to be a king showing his valor, or a household utensil that serves its owner's use, than to be these false gods; better also the door of a house that protects those inside it than these false gods; better also a wooden pillar in a palace than these false gods.

**59** For sun and moon and stars are bright, and obedient in the service for which they are sent.

**60** Likewise the lightning, when it flashes, is widely seen; and the wind blows over every land.

**61** And when God commands the clouds to go over all the earth, they carry out his command.

**62** And the fire, sent down from above to consume mountains and forests, carries out what it is commanded; but these gods are not to be compared to them in appearance or in power.

**63** Therefore one must not think or say that they are gods; they are not able to give judgment or to do good to people.

**64** Knowing then that they are not gods, do not fear them.

**65** They can neither curse kings nor bless them.

**66** They do not show signs in the heaven for the nations, nor do they shine as the sun or give light like the moon.

**67** Wild animals are better than they, for they can flee to shelter and take care of themselves.

**68** So it is in no way evident to us that they are gods; therefore do not fear them.

**69** For like a scarecrow in a cucumber field that protects nothing, so are their gods of wood, silvered and gilded.

**70** In the same way also their wooden, gilded, and silvered gods are like a white thornbush in a garden, on which every bird perches; or like a corpse thrown out in the darkness.

**71** From the purple and linen that rot upon them you will know that they are not gods; and they will themselves in the end be consumed and be a reproach in the land.

**72** Better therefore is the righteous man who has no idols, for he will be far from reproach.

---
*EMET notes: The refrain "from this it is evident that they are not gods; so do not fear them" (v.16, and variants at vv.23, 29, 40, 44, 49, 51, 64, 68, 72) is the structural backbone of the letter. The satire is sophisticated — the idols are not merely useless, they are a source of shame and moral corruption to their priests and worshippers. vv.42-43 the temple prostitution scene is among the most explicit in the Bible. v.54 "burned like beams" — connects to v.8, v.58 where the wood of the idol is emphasized; the idol is ultimately just lumber.*
